analysis.title: September Jobs Preview: Steady as she goes
key_insights: Natixis expects September nonfarm payrolls to slow to +60k from the August pace of 162k, below the 90k consensus, but still a solid gain.
The 60k estimate would bring the three-month moving average of payroll gains to 81k. Payrolls have been volatile this year and mostly surprised to the upside.
Natixis expects very high job gains in leisure and hospitality and local government to fade. It expects solid gains in manufacturing and construction to continue, driven by the data center buildout.
Natixis expects the unemployment rate to rise to a rounded 4.2% on higher participation from prime-age workers. The rate rose 5bps in August despite the strong payrolls number.
Consumers are pessimistic about job prospects and wage gains are tepid, which Natixis reads as underlying softness. Slower labor supply has kept the unemployment rate stable over the past year.
Natixis expects average hourly earnings of about 0.3% m/m in September. A hot reading would be hawkish because it would signal an inflationary impulse from the labor market.

A strong payrolls print alone would not necessarily be hawkish. It would need higher participation, a stable unemployment rate and higher wage gains. Natixis does not expect Friday's data to add pressure for an October hike.
Much weaker than expected jobs data could lower the bar for what counts as an acceptable CPI print on October 14.

Natixis sees a genuine divide on the FOMC over the inflation trajectory and how patient to be. Unless CPI is higher than expected and broad-based, it sees a pause in October and a reassessment in December.
Midterm elections fall less than a week after the October meeting. Natixis does not think the Fed is politically compromised, but says a pause is the prudent path if a hike is a toss-up.
Over the last 10 years, August payrolls have been revised down only once.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong payrolls would still not be hawkish unless accompanied by higher participation, a stable unemployment rate and higher wage gains. Natixis does not expect this week's data to add pressure for an October hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Labor market heating up and adding an inflationary impulse would be hawkish. A genuine FOMC divide on inflation and a hot CPI could tip the Fed toward a hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CPI on October 14 higher than expected and broad-based would undermine the October pause view.
